item.title: School board advances parcel tax, lowers rate
item.description: The Palo Alto Board of Education unanimously voted Tuesday to renew its parcel tax on the June ballot, reducing the rate to $800 per parcel for a period of four years in an effort to sustain community support. The post School board advances parcel tax, lowers rate appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Train hits car near East Meadow crossing
item.description: Two people were reportedly injured after a train hit a vehicle near the East Meadow Drive rail crossing in Palo Alto on Wednesday evening. The post Train hits car near East Meadow crossing appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.description: For many people, Valentine’s Day is a relaxing evening of being wined and dined and sharing a kiss or two. item.title: Esteemed Bay Area chef to debut upscale Mexican restaurant, Amado
item.description: At Amado, not only does the food tell a story, but the plates do as well. The soon-to-open downtown Burlingame restaurant is a love note to Mexican cuisine, offering hard-to-find ancestral dishes, including seven mole variations from various regions. The post Esteemed Bay Area chef to debut upscale Mexican restaurant, Amado appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Liccardo’s bills to speed up housing approvals advance through House
item.description: A pair of bills spearheaded by U.S. Rep. Sam Liccardo that aim to speed up the approval process for new residential projects advanced through the U.S. House of Representatives earlier this week as part of a bipartisan housing package. The bipartisan act aims to alleviate the housing shortage by streamlining housing regulations, updating certain programs in the Department of Housing and Urban Development and modernizing banking regulations to expand lending opportunities.
